symptom: DESCRIBE flattens a microflow whose branches cross into nested ifs that mean something else, and warns MDL-FLOW01 'must not be re-executed' instead of describing it
cause: Nested if/then/else is single-entry/single-exit. A merge reached by branches of two different splits has no place in a tree, so the describer walked past it and emitted the conjunction along one path.
fix: Mode 2: label the shared-suffix entry AND the split's post-dominator, emit `join <label>` at every branch end, then declare each merge as a top-level section after the traversal. MDL-FLOW01 is retired per decision when the description actually declared the merge.
insight: Three traps, each of which produced plausible-looking output. (1) A crossed merge must be emitted the OPPOSITE way from an error-rejoin merge -- rejoin is DECLARED where the traversal meets it, crossed is JOINED by each branch and declared once afterwards -- so the label alone cannot drive emission; carry a crossed set beside the names. (2) Emit the join BEFORE the visited guard: arriving twice is what 'crossed' MEANS, and the guard silently swallows the second branch's join, leaving that path falling off the end. (3) Retire a warning on what was EMITTED, not on what was labelled. An inheritance split has its own traversal that walks through a labelled merge without emitting a join, so the label goes unused and the reader still gets the nested rendering -- suppressing on the label alone silenced MDL-FLOW01 on Administration.ManageMyAccount, whose description is byte-identical with and without the feature. That forced warnings to be computed AFTER the body instead of before it. Method: keep a baseline binary (git stash -u; build) and diff `describe` over every microflow in a corpus -- the refactor step should be byte-identical (it was, 18 of 18) and the feature step should change only the microflows it targets (2 of 18). Anything else changing is the bug.
